Insatsen är en samarbete mellan Norad och Sida med syftet att öka och bredda stödet till det ukrainska civilsamhället. Målet är nå olika typer av organisationer, hålla en geografisk och tematisk bredd och nå de mest utsatta. Programmet kommer att bidra till finansiellt stöd och kapacitetsstöd till CSO:er, till studier samt nätverkande. Implementerande partner är International Renaissance Foundation (IRF) and Ednannia.

The contribution is a Norad-Sida collaboration to increase and broaden the support to the Ukrainian civil society. The aim is to reach different types of organisations, be broad in its geographic and thematic scoop, and reach out to prioritised groups. The programme will contribute to grants, capacity building, research and networking. Implementing partners are International Renaissance Foundation (IRF) and Ednannia.

At at total, more than 263 civil society organisations' work were strengthened through grants and capacity building.
138 CSO's supported through organisational grants. Example of outcome was the empowering of veterans. 5 regional foras united more than 500 veterans, communities and local leaders to build trust and inclusion. This led to a footbool club for veterans with amputation, a symbol for resilience and new beginnings.
27 organisations were supported with advocacy grants in the areas of democratic governance, human rights, recovery, reconstruction and green and environmental protection. At the Ukrainian Recovery Conference 2025 in Rome, the project resulted in a communication platform, Human Capital Podcast, bringing together representatives of government, civil society and business. Other outcomes were strengthened work for women in leadership and the military, children's protection and the development of a state program for volunteering.
20 research grants were supported in order to improve evidence and instruct policy for reform and recovery, for instance in the areas of the rights for children with disabilities, adolescents' online behaviour or rebuilding houses.
9 media grants were supported, as a response to the US withdrawal.
A study "Resilience and participation of CSOs in recovery of territoral communities" was produced.
69 organizations supported through institutional and small grants, including new 24 grantees across 12 regions, with focus on frontline and adjacent territories (Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Sumy, Mykolaiv, Kherson, etc.). Institutional grants strengthen internal governance, financial systems, and strategic planning of key regional CSOs. Small grants empower community-level initiatives in areas such as local resilience, social cohesion, veterans reintegration, and green recovery.
Growing network of partners working toward people-centered recovery and sustainable civic ecosystems in war-affected regions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
